newsitem.title: USA: Fonar says copyright claim reinstated.
newsitem.headline: Fonar says copyright claim reinstated.

text.p: Fonar Corporation's copyright and unfair competition claims against Magnetic Resonance Plus Inc have been reinstated and remanded for further proceedings by the United States Court of Appeals for the second circuit, Fonar said.

The company said the court's decision, handed down on Wednesday, vacated a judgment by the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York which dismissed Fonar's claims against Magnetic Resonance Plus. Fonar sued Magnetic Resonance Plus in March 1993 for allegedly infringing Fonar's copyrighted software and misappropriating trade secrets.
Magnetic Resonance counterclaimed, alleging Fonar violated Federal antitrust laws and tortiously interfered with Magnetic Resonance's contracts and prospective economic advantage.

The District Court dismissed Fonar's claims in July 1996. Fonar appealed and although the appeal was still pending premitted Magnetic Resonance's counterclaims to go to trial in December. The jury found against Fonar on the two tortious interference claims and rejected the antitrust claims.
The appeals court's decision yesterday vacated the District court's order and judgment and remanded the case for further proceedings, Fonar, which makes MRI scanners, said.
